segments.narration: Treasure hunters dynamited them open and found nothing inside.
In the 1930s United Fruit crews clearing jungle for banana plantations in southern Costa Rica started hitting stone balls. Hundreds of them.
Over three hundred are known. The biggest is more than two and a half metres across, about fifteen tons, ground very nearly perfectly round.
Naturally, somebody decided they were full of gold. Crews drilled and dynamited them, and several were gone before authorities stepped in. Solid stone, every one.

The Diquis carved them from about 600 CE until the Spanish arrived, and the evidence is not mystical at all. It is architecture: spheres set in rows along the path to a chief's house, so you knew whose land you stood on.
